newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- US T-bonds setting up for decisive turn.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- US T-bonds setting up for decisive turn.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures are poised for a sharp move regardless of which way Federal Reserve policymakers lean Tuesday, technical analysts said.

Three weeks of consolidation around 110-00 in June futures have left market participants eager to jump on the next trend, and analysts believe the Federal Open Market Committee's decision will provide the catalyst.
"We're going to move with some authority after the meeting tomorrow," predicted Donald Pullen, bond analyst for ED&F Man on the floor of the Chicago Board of Trade.
What is less clear is the direction prices will take.

Analysts said a selloff was likely to follow an increase in the Fed funds target because a 25 basis point hike was not currently factored into prices. The market is evenly split on the odds U.S. central bankers will tighten credit on Tuesday.
"If the Fed does nothing, the market will respond very positively," Pullen said. If it raises rates, he said, look for heavy selling.
Depending on the Fed's action, Pullen said June bond futures would violate either resistance at 110-22 or support at 109-02 and then extend the trend two full points from the breakout.
"All this consolidation suggests we're going to make a trend move, and the catalyst will be tomorrow's FOMC meeting," the analyst said.
With the countdown to the meeting under way, June bond futures were stalled, trading 3/32 lower at 109-28 at midday.

If the central bank takes no action Tuesday, traders will view it as a delay and will sell in anticipation of future rate increases, predicted Nick Kalivas, senior credit market analyst for Refco Inc.
"No matter what happens tomorrow, I think the market will go down," he said.

Kalivas said June bond futures would find solid support in the 108-00 handle, setting the stage longer term for a test of channel resistance and a possible upside breakout. He saw layers of support at 108-30, 108-20 and 108-08 cushioning a fall.

June futures have spent most of May consolidating near the top of a well-defined downward channel that has guided the market since early December, after rejecting the base in a powerful late-April rally, Kalivas noted.
"The work that we've done is an indication that we could reverse the downtrend," Kalivas said.
A settlement above 111-01 would confirm an upside breakout and pave the way for a test of 113-25, the February 18 high, he said.
